record_title: Square-root Rankin-Cohen independence for quadratic twists
scientific_context: For a fixed odd fundamental discriminant D, the recent theorem of Takloo-Bighash proves linear independence of the first r traced diagonal Rankin-Cohen brackets for each fixed r and sufficiently large weight. This result permits r to grow at the square-root scale: for every c<(2*pi*e*|D|)^(-1/2), the first floor(c*sqrt(ell)) brackets are independent for all sufficiently large admissible ell. The proof applies an exact Mobius-inversion column transform to the Fourier endpoint matrix, producing an ordinary Vandermonde before estimating the explicit coefficient remainder.
limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. D is fixed and odd; there is no uniformity in growing |D|. The result does not reach a positive proportion of the full level-one eigenbasis, does not settle the conjectural linear-size Rankin-Cohen independence program, and does not claim the constant (2*pi*e*|D|)^(-1/2) is optimal. For D=1, Luo's 2015 theorem already gives a stronger linear-order nonvanishing count, so the new D=1 content is the explicit square-root Rankin-Cohen independence. Luo's full text was not inspected here; its abstract and later literature's description were inspected. Unindexed concurrent work around the September 2026 motivating preprint remains a residual originality risk. The finite exact verification is corroborative only. No independent validation, independent audit, or formal proof-assistant verification is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone Python 3 exact-integer verification of the Mobius-inversion column transform and Vandermonde determinant for D=1 and for the quadratic character modulo 5, including character zeros.
